card.name: Distributive words after quantities
card.fires_on: The word right after a number or amount, such as each, mg, days, doses or three, where the amount is being spread over items, times or periods.

modes.label: Unit after a dose number
modes.description: The unit mg or a word like doses or days directly follows a number in a list of amounts or durations.
modes.example: A male patient took 120 mg per day for four days, then 180 mg per day for seven<< days>>.

modes.label: Each after a quantity
modes.description: The word each follows a count or volume to say the amount applies per item or per time.
modes.example: Immediately rinse twice with 30 mL<< each>> time to ensure that no residue remains in

modes.label: Count word in a range
modes.description: A number word or plus sign follows a number or range as the amount continues.
modes.example: 00 mg to 600 mg<< three>> times a day.

card.writes: It seems to favor Chinese words for amounts and totals, and to suppress Chinese and Japanese words meaning respectively or among which.
card.plain: It fires on the word that comes right after a number, such as each, mg or days, when amounts are being listed.
